| 12 | Visualize without chaos |
| **13** | Tell one honest data story |

## Checkpoint D (today)

**Bigger practical + short presentation (~3–5 min)**

Not a methods olympiad — a **communication** checkpoint.

## Required beats

1. Biological / ecological question
2. What you loaded & how you cleaned/joined it
3. **One primary figure** (+ optional QC inset)
4. What the figure does **not** show

## Practical workflow (use this checklist)

1. Reload data with your Week 11 checks
2. Choose aggregation (top taxa / taxonomic level)
3. Make 1–2 candidate figures; pick the clearest
4. Write a 2–3 sentence caption
5. List assumptions (relative vs absolute, filters, batch, …)

## Good Checkpoint D topics (examples)

- Composition shift across sites / hosts / time
- A treatment contrast visible at phylum level
- Dominants vs rare “Other” fraction
- Library-size QC that changes interpretation

## Grading emphasis

| Higher weight | Lower weight |
|---|---|
| Clear question + readable figure | Exotic ordinations |
| Correct joins / labeled axes | Dozens of panels |
| Honest limits | Decorative colour |

## Bridge across the semester

You started with **models from tiny time series**.

You end the content blocks by **reading complex ecological tables** — the skill working biologists actually need on day one of a microbiome project.

## Looking ahead

**Week 14 (17 Dec):** synthesis wrap — connect Checkpoints A–D; optional portfolio polish.

## Exit ticket

1. What is your one-sentence claim?
2. What would make you distrust your own figure?
3. Which earlier checkpoint skill did you reuse (loop? replicate thinking? model vs data honesty?)?
